## Best Payment Gateway for D2C India: A Practical Guide for 2026

The best payment gateway for a D2C brand in India is usually the one that supports UPI, cards, net banking, wallets, refunds and reliable settlement without creating reconciliation problems. For most growing brands, Razorpay, Cashfree Payments, PayU, PhonePe Payment Gateway and CCAvenue are worth comparing, but the right choice depends on your platform, average order value, COD share, subscription model and customer profile.

A payment gateway is not just a button on the checkout page. It affects how easily customers pay, how quickly your team receives money, how failed transactions are handled and how accurately orders are matched with settlements.

This guide compares the main options for Indian D2C brands in 2026. It focuses on practical buying decisions rather than presenting one gateway as suitable for every business.

## What D2C Brands Should Expect from a Payment Gateway

D2C businesses typically sell through a website, mobile storefront, social media campaigns, marketplaces or a combination of these channels. A payment gateway needs to work across this environment and handle both first-time and returning customers.

Indian buyers may use UPI for a low-value purchase, a credit card for a larger order, a saved card for a repeat transaction or cash on delivery when they are unsure about the brand. Your checkout should not assume that every buyer prefers the same payment method.

A suitable gateway should support:

- UPI collect or intent-based payments, where available
- UPI AutoPay or recurring payment options for eligible use cases
- Credit and debit cards issued in India and, where relevant, international cards
- Net banking
- Common wallets and other supported instruments
- Refunds through the merchant dashboard or API
- Webhooks for payment status updates
- Payment links for WhatsApp, Instagram or assisted sales
- Plugins for platforms such as Shopify, WooCommerce, Magento and custom websites
- Settlement reports and downloadable transaction data
- Fraud and risk controls
- Customer support for failed payments and account issues

The gateway also needs to suit your operational maturity. A small brand may value a simple plugin and easy dashboard. A larger D2C business may need APIs, multiple stores, automated reconciliation and controls for refunds by user or order status.

### Gateway, payment aggregator or checkout platform?

The terms are often used interchangeably, but they describe different layers.

A payment gateway technically connects your website or app to banks and payment networks. A payment aggregator may provide the merchant onboarding, payment collection and settlement relationship as one service. A checkout platform can add features such as address intelligence, one-click payments, offer management or improved checkout flows.

For a D2C brand, the practical question is not the terminology. Ask who is responsible for onboarding, settlement, refunds, payment disputes, technical integration and support.

## The Main Payment Gateway Options in India

The following providers are commonly considered by Indian online businesses. Features, pricing, onboarding requirements and product availability can change, so confirm the current terms directly before signing up.

### Razorpay

Razorpay is widely used by startups, online retailers, service businesses and technology companies. It offers payment collection tools, APIs, payment links, subscriptions and dashboard-based operations.

It is often considered by D2C brands that want:

- A familiar integration ecosystem
- WooCommerce, Shopify or custom API options
- Payment links for social and assisted selling
- Automated payment status updates through webhooks
- Subscription or recurring payment capabilities
- Developer documentation and operational dashboards

The important evaluation point is not only whether the gateway accepts payments. Check how it handles payment failures, refund requests, settlement reports and customer support during account or transaction issues.

### Cashfree Payments

Cashfree Payments is another major option for online businesses. It is commonly evaluated for payment collection, payouts, recurring payments, verification workflows and marketplace-related use cases.

It may suit D2C brands that need:

- Payment gateway and payout services from one provider
- APIs for a custom storefront or mobile application
- Recurring payment support for memberships or replenishment products
- Detailed transaction and settlement information
- Payment links or hosted payment options
- Support for businesses operating more than one sales channel

If your business will use payouts to delivery partners, affiliates, vendors or creators, ask whether combining collections and payouts will simplify your finance operations or create an unnecessary dependency on one provider.

### PayU

PayU is used by online merchants across e-commerce, education, financial services and other sectors. It has a broad payments offering and is often considered by businesses looking for an established provider with support for multiple payment methods.

For a D2C business, evaluate:

- Whether the required checkout and API features are available for your business category
- The quality of platform plugins or custom integration support
- Refund and dispute workflows
- Settlement reporting
- International card acceptance, if needed
- Account management and escalation processes

A large provider can be useful, but your internal team should still test the dashboard and reporting before committing.

### PhonePe Payment Gateway

PhonePe is a major consumer payments brand in India and offers payment gateway services to merchants. Its brand familiarity can be relevant when a significant share of your customers prefer UPI.

It can be worth evaluating when:

- UPI is a major payment method for your customers
- You want to assess a recognisable consumer payment experience
- Your business needs standard card, net banking and UPI acceptance
- You are comparing direct and aggregator-led payment relationships
- Your website or app requires API integration

Do not select a gateway only because customers know the consumer brand. Compare the merchant dashboard, refund process, settlement files, support and integration effort as carefully as the customer-facing checkout.

### CCAvenue

CCAvenue has been a long-standing payment gateway option in India and supports a broad range of payment methods and merchant categories.

It may be considered by brands that want:

- A mature payment gateway provider
- Multiple payment methods
- Support for online retail and service businesses
- Hosted checkout and integration options
- A provider with experience across different types of merchants

For a modern D2C operation, test how easily the gateway fits into your store platform and whether the reporting is convenient for your finance team. A gateway can support many methods but still require manual work if its exports do not match your order and accounting systems.

### Other options

Depending on your model, you may also review BillDesk, Worldline, Easebuzz, Paytm-related merchant payment products where available, and specialist checkout or payment providers. Banks may offer direct payment gateway arrangements for some businesses.

The shortlist should be based on fit rather than brand recognition. A provider that is suitable for a large marketplace may not offer the simplest onboarding or reporting for a small skincare brand, school merchandise store or regional food business.

## Comparison of Payment Gateways for D2C Brands

| Provider | Often considered for | Strengths to evaluate | Questions to ask before choosing |
|---|---|---|---|
| Razorpay | Startups, D2C websites, SaaS and service businesses | Broad ecosystem, APIs, payment links, subscriptions, common plugins | How are settlement reports, refunds and support handled for your account? |
| Cashfree Payments | D2C brands, marketplaces, businesses needing payouts | Payment collection, payouts, APIs and recurring payment use cases | Will collections and payouts integrate cleanly with your finance workflow? |
| PayU | Established online merchants and multi-category businesses | Multiple payment methods, merchant infrastructure and integrations | What onboarding, support and reporting arrangements apply to your business? |
| PhonePe Payment Gateway | Brands with strong UPI demand | Familiar UPI brand and online payment capabilities | Does the merchant dashboard and integration meet your operational needs? |
| CCAvenue | Businesses seeking a mature, broad payment offering | Long-standing presence and multiple payment methods | Is the checkout and reconciliation experience convenient for your team? |
| Bank or specialist provider | Businesses with specific pricing, risk or integration requirements | May suit a particular industry or transaction profile | Who manages integration, disputes, refunds and technical support? |

This table is a starting point, not a ranking. Payment gateway performance can vary by transaction type, bank, device, payment method, network conditions and customer location.

## The Features That Matter Most in 2026

### UPI performance and payment status handling

UPI is central to Indian online payments, but a UPI transaction can still fail because of bank downtime, app switching, customer limits, delayed confirmation or a session timeout.

Your gateway should provide clear payment statuses, including successful, failed, pending and expired transactions. It should also send server-to-server confirmation through webhooks rather than relying only on the customer returning to your website.

This matters because a customer may complete payment but close the browser before returning to the order confirmation page. Your system should verify the gateway status before marking the order as paid or releasing it for dispatch.

### Cards and tokenisation

Cards remain important for higher-value orders, repeat purchases and customers who prefer credit card rewards or EMI options. Indian card transactions use tokenisation requirements and other controls intended to protect card information.

Your brand should avoid storing raw card details. Confirm that the gateway and your e-commerce platform handle tokenised card data appropriately and that your checkout does not expose sensitive payment information.

If you sell products with higher average order values, ask about supported card networks, international cards, EMI availability and additional authentication requirements. These features may depend on your merchant category, bank arrangements and gateway approval.

### Recurring payments and subscriptions

Recurring billing can be useful for subscription boxes, memberships, donations, software access, supplements and replenishment products. It also introduces additional compliance and customer-consent requirements.

Ask the gateway:

- Which recurring payment methods are supported?
- How is customer consent recorded?
- How are mandates created, paused and cancelled?
- How are failed renewals communicated?
- Can customers update their payment method?
- How are refunds and partial cancellations handled?

Do not build a subscription model around a feature that the gateway supports only in a limited form. Test the full lifecycle before launch, including missed payments and cancellation requests.

### Payment links and social selling

Many Indian D2C brands receive orders through Instagram, WhatsApp, phone calls, exhibitions and creator campaigns. Payment links can help collect money without sending every buyer through the full website checkout.

A useful payment link feature should allow you to:

- Set the amount and order reference
- Share the link over WhatsApp, SMS or social channels
- Track whether the link was paid
- Expire or deactivate old links
- Issue a receipt or payment confirmation
- Match the payment to the customer and order

Payment links are convenient, but they can create reconciliation issues if staff members generate links without a standard naming or order-number process.

### Refunds, disputes and chargebacks

Refunds are routine in D2C e-commerce. Customers may cancel before dispatch, receive a damaged item, return a product or be charged for an order that was not created correctly.

Review the complete refund workflow:

- Can your team issue full and partial refunds?
- Can refunds be linked to an order ID?
- How long does the refund usually take to reach the customer?
- Is the refund status visible in the dashboard?
- Can your accounting team export refund data?
- What happens when a customer raises a card dispute?

The time taken for a refund to reach a customer can depend on the payment method, issuing bank and banking network. Communicate this clearly in your refund policy rather than promising that every refund will appear immediately.

## How Much Does a Payment Gateway Cost?

Payment gateway pricing usually depends on the payment method, transaction value, merchant category, business risk, expected volume, settlement arrangement and whether you need additional products.

Common cost components can include:

- A percentage-based transaction fee
- GST on applicable gateway fees
- Different rates for domestic and international cards
- Separate terms for wallets, EMI or other payment methods
- Subscription or recurring payment charges
- Refund or chargeback-related charges in some arrangements
- Optional costs for premium checkout, analytics or payment links
- One-time integration or setup charges in certain contracts

UPI pricing and merchant charges can depend on the specific payment instrument and regulatory or commercial arrangements in force at the time. Do not assume that every UPI transaction has the same cost as a card transaction.

Ask for a written commercial proposal that clearly shows whether rates are inclusive or exclusive of GST. Also ask whether the quoted rate applies to all transactions or only to a particular volume band.

A lower transaction fee is not always the lowest total cost. Consider the cost of:

- Failed payments that are not retried properly
- Manual settlement matching
- Staff time spent checking payment screenshots
- Delayed refunds
- Technical maintenance
- Separate tools for payouts, subscriptions or fraud review
- Lost orders caused by unclear payment statuses

### A simple cost comparison method

Take a representative month and list:

1. Total successful online order value
2. Number of online orders
3. Share of UPI, cards, net banking and other methods
4. Number of refunds
5. International transaction share, if any
6. COD orders that you hope to convert to prepaid
7. Time spent by finance staff on reconciliation

Then request a quote using this profile. A gateway comparison based only on a public headline rate may not reflect your actual cost.

## Checkout Integration for Indian D2C Stores

The best payment gateway for D2C India is one that fits your existing technology without making routine operations difficult.

### Shopify

Shopify stores generally use an available payment app or provider integration. Check whether the provider supports your store configuration, refund workflow, order status updates and payment method requirements.

Before going live, test:

- Successful UPI payments
- Failed and abandoned payments
- Card authentication
- Full and partial refunds
- Payment captured but order not updated
- Duplicate payment attempts
- COD and prepaid order separation

### WooCommerce

WooCommerce offers more flexibility, but plugin quality matters. A payment plugin should be maintained, compatible with your WordPress and WooCommerce versions, and configured securely.

Do not install several overlapping payment plugins without a plan. Conflicting checkout scripts can slow down the page or create duplicate payment attempts. Keep plugins updated and use a staging environment when possible.

### Custom websites and mobile apps

A custom store may provide better control over checkout, but it requires more development responsibility. Your developer must implement signature verification, webhook handling, idempotency, error states and secure refund workflows.

Never mark an order as paid solely because a customer reaches a success URL. Verify the payment on the server using the gateway's approved method.

For a mobile app, also test app switching during UPI payments, deep-link behaviour and what happens when the user returns after a delay.

### Multiple gateways

Some established D2C brands use more than one payment gateway. This may provide operational resilience or access to different payment methods, but it also increases complexity.

You may need to manage:

- Multiple dashboards
- Different settlement cycles
- Different refund procedures
- Separate webhook formats
- Multiple reconciliation files
- Different support escalation routes

Use multiple gateways only when there is a clear business reason. A poorly managed multi-gateway setup can create more errors than it solves.

## Compliance, Security and Finance Checks

An Indian D2C brand should treat payment setup as a compliance and finance project, not only a website task.

### Business and KYC documents

Payment providers usually require business, bank and tax documentation as part of merchant onboarding. Requirements vary by business structure and risk category.

Keep the following information ready where applicable:

- PAN and business registration details
- GST registration details, if registered or required
- Bank account proof
- Address proof
- Website, refund and privacy policies
- Product and pricing information
- Beneficial ownership or director details for relevant entities

Your legal business name, bank account name, website footer and invoices should not create avoidable inconsistencies.

### RBI and payment security requirements

The Reserve Bank of India regulates important aspects of payment systems and payment aggregators. Requirements can change, so your provider should explain the applicable onboarding, settlement, card-data and recurring-payment processes.

For card payments, use the gateway's hosted or tokenised flow instead of handling raw card data yourself. Confirm who is responsible for the relevant security controls and what your website or app must do.

Also review:

- HTTPS and valid SSL configuration
- Admin access controls
- Two-factor authentication
- Webhook signature verification
- API key storage
- Logs and audit trails
- Payment data retention
- Role-based refund permissions

### GST invoices and accounting

A payment gateway does not replace your invoicing and accounting system. Your order system should generate the appropriate invoice and record the payment method, transaction reference, tax amount, refund and final order status.

Make sure your reports distinguish between:

- Gross order value
- Discounts
- Shipping charges
- GST collected on the sale
- Gateway fees
- GST charged on gateway fees
- Refunds
- Net settlement received
- COD remittances
- Payment disputes

Your accountant may need gateway settlement reports, bank statements and order exports together. Set up a repeatable monthly reconciliation process rather than trying to reconstruct transactions at the end of the financial year.

## How to Select the Right Gateway

Use a shortlisting process that reflects your actual customer and operations.

### Step 1: Measure your payment mix

Review the last few months, if you are already selling online. Identify the share of prepaid, COD, UPI, cards, net banking and international transactions.

If you are a new brand, use your expected product price and customer segment as a starting assumption, but do not treat it as a guaranteed forecast.

### Step 2: Define the must-have features

Separate essential requirements from optional ones.

For example, a regional apparel brand may need UPI, cards, COD reconciliation and WhatsApp payment links. A subscription food business may additionally need recurring mandates, automated retries and customer self-service. A luxury D2C brand may prioritise international cards, fraud review and high-value order controls.

### Step 3: Test the full order lifecycle

Do not stop after making one successful test payment. Test:

- Payment success
- Payment failure
- Pending payment
- Customer closes the payment window
- Duplicate payment
- Full refund
- Partial refund
- Cancelled order after payment
- Webhook delay
- Bank or app interruption
- Failed recurring charge, if applicable

Record what the customer sees and what your operations team sees.

### Step 4: Review reconciliation

Download sample reports and match them against your order system. Check whether the report includes order ID, gateway transaction ID, settlement reference, amount, fee, GST, refund and settlement date.

If your finance team cannot easily match the data, the problem will grow with transaction volume.

### Step 5: Compare support and account management

Ask who will handle:

- Onboarding delays
- Payment failures
- Settlement holds
- Refund questions
- Technical incidents
- Disputes and chargebacks
- Changes to your business model

Get escalation contacts and response expectations in writing. Do not rely only on a sales conversation.

## Frequently Asked Questions

### Which is the best payment gateway for a small D2C business in India?

There is no single best option for every small business. Razorpay, Cashfree Payments, PayU, PhonePe Payment Gateway and CCAvenue are reasonable providers to compare, especially if you need UPI, cards, refunds and a standard e-commerce integration.

Choose based on onboarding, settlement reporting, support, total cost and integration quality rather than the provider's name alone.

### Is Razorpay better than Cashfree for D2C brands?

Both can be suitable, but the better choice depends on your requirements. Compare their current commercial terms, checkout integration, payment links, subscription features, support process, settlement reports and payout requirements.

Run the same test cases on both if your business is expected to process meaningful order volume.

### Do D2C brands still need COD if they offer online payments?

COD can remain relevant in India, particularly for new brands, certain regions and customers who are cautious about prepaid orders. However, COD can increase return-to-origin costs and operational work.

Track COD acceptance, cancellation and return rates by location and product. You can then decide whether to encourage prepaid orders through clear policies, payment offers or a better checkout experience.

### How quickly are payment gateway settlements received?

Settlement timing depends on the provider agreement, business category, payment method, risk review, bank holidays and any reserve or verification requirements. Do not assume that all payment methods settle on the same schedule.

Ask for the standard settlement cycle, the conditions that can delay settlement and the format of settlement reports before launch.

### Can a payment gateway reduce failed online payments?

A gateway cannot eliminate all failures because bank outages, customer limits, network issues and authentication problems remain possible. It may reduce avoidable failures through better checkout design, payment-method coverage, clear status handling and suitable retry or fallback flows.

Monitor failure rates by payment method, bank, device and error reason. This gives you a more useful view than looking only at the overall payment success rate.

### Should a D2C business use one gateway or two?

One gateway is simpler to integrate, reconcile and support. Two gateways may be justified when you have substantial volume, a clear resilience requirement or materially different payment needs.

Start with one well-tested provider unless a second gateway solves a specific operational problem. If you add another, define which transactions use each gateway and how refunds and reconciliation will work.

## Where to Start

Make a shortlist of two or three providers based on your store platform, payment mix, average order value and need for subscriptions or payment links. Request current commercial terms, GST treatment, settlement details and onboarding requirements in writing.

Then complete a test plan covering UPI, cards, failed payments, refunds, webhooks, order updates and settlement reconciliation. Confirm that your website has clear shipping, cancellation, refund, privacy and contact information before applying.
